correctness.rationale: Valid positive binary strings have language 1(1|00)*. Length-m suffix-value lists V_m split in increasing numerical order as V_(m−2) concatenated with 2^(m−1)+V_(m−1), and hence internal gaps W_m split into W_(m−2), one bridge G_m, W_(m−1). A fixed G_m bridge occurs F_(L−m) times inside positive support elements of binary length L, and all length-boundary gaps alternate between 1 and 2. Summation L=m+1..K gives F_(K−m+2)−1; prefix support count F_(K+2) and gap count F_(K+2)−1. G2=G3=3 and others distinct; Fibonacci ratios give limiting point masses and exact geometric tail. Since G_m grows like 2^m and φ<2 the mean diverges. Direct independent binary predicate against complete histogram for K=1..16 passed. These prefix checks do not prove unbounded K or the tail law.

value.rationale: The complete return gap spectrum and exact dyadic-prefix probability law describe a natural and mathematically useful recurrence invariant of a classical automatic sequence. Heavy tail and infinite mean despite structured Fibonacci support growth is a notable sharp classification, with clear sampling convention and exact finite histogram.

final_claim: For the Baum–Sweet support 0=s0<s1<… the dyadic-prefix adjacent-return gap histogram has exact values N_K(g) from bridge lengths G_m=2^(m−2)+1+1_(2|m) and Fibonacci multiplicities; the limiting gap law has P(3)=φ^-1, P(G_m)=φ^-m (m≥4), exact tail φ^(2−m), exponent log_2 φ and infinite mean.
limitations: Support includes 0, and the finite histogram requires both endpoints inside the dyadic prefix.
G2=G3=3 is a duplicated bridge value; summed mass P(3)=φ^-1.
A finite histogram alone is not an exhaustion argument for the full infinite spectrum.
